doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Authenticity and pop music versus jazz
summary: Smith says pop was always the popular music and jazz a minority interest.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You know there is an authenticity that is at the heart of the best jazz music that I’ve heard or participated in. And something that alarms me is that in some of today’s pop music I feel like they’re playing chords or they’re singing lyrics just to sell an album and I don’t feel sometimes that the musicians have experienced what it is that they’re saying or playing. You know? And do you see any young artists today that are bringing any of that authenticity back?

Well, that’s hard for me to say. I must admit I’ve been as guilty as others my age that I’ve really turned away from that music because I don’t find anything that reflects my ideas. But you know, my children respect me for what I do, but they’ve got their own kind of music, and it’s today’s music. I can’t really answer your question. There are young players who play jazz, I mean I see them all the time. But I think their roots are in the music that we played, and so they’re carrying on and developing that tradition. Some of the newer music I find difficult to listen to. When it comes to pop music, I’ve often gone into this argument and say well pop music now is so terrible. But pop music has always been exactly that. It’s been the popular music of the age. I don’t think jazz was ever the popular music of the age. It was always a minority interest. And so we get together and have these discussions about it and put down rap music, but you know there was so much in the ‘20’s and ‘30’s of moon and June and spoon, and really dumb things, and we just accepted it because we were young then. But it’s no better or worse, it’s just the popular music of the time. I don’t think jazz was ever the popular music of the time. I mean maybe swing in the ‘40’s I suppose—
Yeah, that was more of a dance — there wasn’t nearly as much improvisation — it was more arranged.
